cohort: The study included all cases undergoing ex-utero intrapartum treatment (EXIT) procedures at a tertiary obstetric unit between 1997 and 2020.
finding: Risks for neonatal demise following an EXIT procedure include fetal teratoma, low birth weight, and prematurity; micrognathia is an increasingly valid indication, especially when combined with polyhydramnios and an inferior facial angle (IFA) <5%, which correlates with severe airway obstruction.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was noted as a factor in 75% of neonates with fetal teratoma.
gest_age: Preterm labor and prematurity were identified as factors, with 75% of fetal teratoma cases presenting with preterm premature rupture of membranes or preterm labor.
